sections.h2: Where is the Jackson County Recorder, and when is it open?
sections.html:
The Jackson County Recorder is on the third floor of the Jackson County Courthouse, 226 East Main Street, Jackson, OH 45640. Call (740) 286-1919 or fax (740) 286-8835. The county page gives hours of Monday through Friday, 8:30 am to 4:00 pm, and says the office closes from 11:30 am until 12:30 pm for lunch.

The office accepts cash, check and debit or credit card, and charges a $2.00 service fee when a card is used. Jackson County's official records begin in 1997. Earlier documents have to be viewed and printed at the office, while most later records can be searched online after setting up an account.

sections.h2: What does the Jackson County Recorder charge?
sections.html:
The Recorder's fee page lists $39.00 for the first two pages of a deed, mortgage, lease, affidavit or most other recordable documents, plus $8.00 for each page after that. The page notes that each printed side counts as one page. The county says Ohio sets the fees, with half going to the basic recording fee and half to the Ohio Housing Trust Fund.

ItemFee
Deed, mortgage or lease, first two pages$39.00
Each added page$8.00
Marginal notation (release, assignment, amendment)$4.00 each
Plat or condominium drawing, per 8 by 14 sheet$40.00
UCC financing statement tied to real estate$12.00 plus $4.00 per name indexed
Copy$2.00 per page
Certified copy$2.00 per page plus $1.00 for the seal

Source: Jackson County Recorder fee page. A veteran's service discharge and one certified copy carry no fee, and zoning resolutions cost $50.00.

sections.h2: What does the Jackson County Auditor collect on a sale?
sections.html:
The Auditor's real estate transfers page lists a conveyance fee of $4.00 per thousand dollars and a transfer fee of $0.50 per parcel. It adds a short history: on March 24, 1993, the conveyance fee rose from $1.00 per thousand of the purchase price to $4.00.

The Auditor sits at 226 East Main Street, Suite 5, in the same courthouse building, with phone (740) 286-4231 and hours of 8:00 am to 4:00 pm. The Auditor's website also carries a Conveyance Calculator and a Sales Reports page under its Tools menu. R.C. 319.202(D) puts the fee on the grantor.

The forms the office posts are:

  • DTE 100, the conveyance fee statement of value and receipt
  • DTE 100EX, the statement of reason for exemption from the fee
  • DTE 100M and 100MEX for manufactured or mobile homes

The sequence is Auditor first, Recorder second. The Recorder's website says that adding or removing a name from title requires a new deed that goes through the Auditor's transfer step and then to recording.

sections.h2: Why does a Jackson County deed have to be recorded?
sections.html:
Because an unrecorded deed loses to a later buyer who did not know about it. R.C. 5301.25 requires deeds and similar instruments to be recorded in the county where the land lies, and until they are, they count as fraudulent as to a later bona fide purchaser without knowledge.

Jackson County's Recorder offers a few plain answers on its site worth knowing before a sale:

  • Most records are public. Military service records are the exception and are released only to the veteran with proof of ID.
  • A will is recorded through Probate Court, at a cost the Recorder's page gives as $46.00.
  • The office recommends an attorney or other professional to prepare deeds and similar legal papers.

If a name has to come off the title, the answer is a new deed, not a note on the old one. The Recorder's site says an owner who adds or removes someone from a deed must create and submit a new deed for transfer at the Auditor's office and then for recording.

sections.h2: How do I get copies or search Jackson County records?
sections.html:
The county Recorder's page directs users to set up an account to view most records online. Official records start in 1997, so a deed from the 1980s or earlier is a trip to the courthouse.

To order a document image, email the book and page of the requested document to the Recorder's office address, recordersoffice@jacksoncounty.us. The cost is $2.00 per page, paid by cash or check. Copies handed over at the counter cost the same $2.00 per page that the fee page lists.

A seller who wants to compare prices before listing can use the Auditor's Sales Reports page, which sits next to the Conveyance Calculator and the Tax Estimator.

sections.h2: What other papers does the Jackson County Recorder file, and at what price?
sections.html:
The fee page covers more than deeds. These listed fees come up when a house has liens or a prior owner left paperwork behind:

  • federal tax liens and other federal liens: $5.00
  • releases or partial releases of those liens: $3.00
  • a living will or durable power of attorney for health care: $40.00
  • zoning amendments: $20.00
  • personal property tax liens, workers' compensation liens, certificates of premium due, recognizance liens and unemployment compensation liens: no fee

The county says each fee is set by Ohio law under R.C. 317.32 and 317.36. A seller who learns of an old lien during a title search should ask the Recorder which release applies and what it costs, since a release is a separate recording from the deed itself.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Jackson County itself?
sections.html:
Jackson County was founded on March 1, 1818 and is named for Andrew Jackson. Wikipedia calls it the Little Wales of Ohio, and its history centers on the Hanging Rock Iron Region. The Jefferson Iron Furnace was built in 1854, and iron from the county went into the USS Monitor. Coal and salt mining followed. Remnants of the furnaces stand in Jackson Lake State Park, and part of Wayne National Forest lies in the county.

The Census Bureau puts July 2025 population at 32,817. QuickFacts shows 14,665 housing units, 73.9% owner-occupied, a median owner-occupied value of $150,700 and a median household income of $57,106. Mean travel time to work is 29.4 minutes, the longest of the four Ohio counties on that comparison, and 15.5% of residents are in poverty. The Auditor's site counts 28,916 parcels for 2024 and 422 square miles of total area.

faqs.q: How much does the Jackson County Recorder charge for a three-page deed?
faqs.a: The fee page lists $39.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each page after that. Ask the Recorder whether a marginal notation applies to your paper, since each adds $4.00.

faqs.q: Does the Jackson County Recorder close for lunch?
faqs.a: Yes. The county's Recorder page says the office is closed from 11:30 am until 12:30 pm, and that its hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 am to 4:00 pm.

faqs.q: How much is the Jackson County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: The Auditor's page lists $4.00 per thousand dollars of the purchase price plus a $0.50 per parcel transfer fee. The fee has been $4.00 per thousand since March 24, 1993.

faqs.q: Is there a charge to pay the Jackson County Recorder with a card?
faqs.a: Yes. The Recorder's site says the office takes debit and credit and adds a $2.00 service fee for card use. Cash and check have no such charge.

faqs.q: Can I record a will with the Jackson County Recorder?
faqs.a: No. The Recorder's site says a will is recorded in Probate Court, and it lists the cost as $46.00. The Recorder handles deeds, mortgages and similar land records.
